name: Sugar Cookies
summary: Rolled sugar cookies, after Fannie Farmer's 1896 method. Branches on how you cream the butter.

equipment.prompt: How are you creaming the butter?
equipment.help: Creaming is the step that decides the texture, and each tool asks for a different touch.
equipment.label: Method

steps.title: Soften the butter
steps.body: Let the butter come to room temperature. Cold butter will not cream.

steps.title: Cream in a stand mixer
steps.body: Use the paddle on medium for three minutes, scraping the bowl twice. Stop when it is pale and fluffy.

steps.title: Cream with a hand mixer
steps.body: Beat on medium for four or five minutes, moving the beaters around the bowl.

steps.title: Cream by hand
steps.body: Work the butter and sugar against the side of the bowl with a wooden spoon until pale. It takes a good ten minutes.

steps.title: Add the egg and milk
steps.body: Beat in the egg, then the milk. The mixture may look curdled; the flour will bring it back.

steps.title: Mix the dry ingredients
steps.body: Stir the flour, baking powder, salt and nutmeg together in a second bowl.

steps.title: Combine
steps.body: Add the dry ingredients to the creamed mixture and stir only until no flour shows.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.body: Cover and chill until firm enough to roll.

steps.title: Heat the oven to 375°F
steps.body: Line two baking sheets while it heats.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.body: Roll the dough a quarter inch thick on a floured board and cut it into rounds. Sprinkle each with sugar.

steps.title: Bake
steps.body: Bake until the edges are just brown. They firm up as they cool.

steps.title: Cool and store
steps.body: Lift onto a rack to cool, then keep in a tin.
